name: SEQSCHED — Svc.SeqScheduler on Ref (TestDeploymentsProject/Ref) — L0: desk-checked; bench confirmation pending
deployment: TestDeploymentsProject/Ref (native Linux host) with harness component Ref.TimeBaseOverride between the topology and Svc.PosixTime

event_patterns.CdhCore.cmdDisp.NoOpStringReceived: Received a NO-OP string=(?P<id>\d+)$|Received a NO-OP string=(?P<message>\S+)$
event_patterns.seqScheduler.RowSkippedNoBase: Row (?P<index>\d+) skipped: time base (?P<timeBase>\w+) never seen$
event_patterns.timeBaseOverride.OverrideChanged: Time base override changed from (?P<previous>\w+) to (?P<current>\w+)$
event_patterns.timeBaseOverride.InvalidTimeBase: Time base (?P<timeBase>\w+) cannot be an override$
event_patterns.FileHandling.prmDb.PrmFileSaveComplete: Parameter file save completed. Wrote (?P<records>\d+) records.$

std_complete: commands_sent == count(event CdhCore.cmdDisp.OpCodeDispatched) - count(sequence-issued NO-OPs) (check function commands_sent_minus_seq)
scope: - UUT: `Svc.SeqScheduler` (lestarch-autobot/fprime `seq-scheduler`), SHA recorded in the manifest at stage 2; constants `SeqSchedulerRows = 8`, `SeqSchedulerSequenceNameSize = 80`.

- Deployment: `TestDeploymentsProject/Ref` **system deployment** plus `seqScheduler: Svc.SeqScheduler` on `rateGroup1Comp` slot 8 (1 Hz) wired to `cmdSeq` and the DataProducts subtopology, and the harness component `timeBaseOverride: Ref.TimeBaseOverride` between the topology's `time connections` and `posixTime` (delta in `Ref/docs/seq-scheduler-topology.md`).
- Bench: native Linux host (no board, no shared bench); Ref and the GDS run on the same host; FSW time = host UNIX time in `TB_WORKSTATION_TIME`.
- Ground system: fprime-gds (harness skill default) through the `fth` pytest plugin; dictionary from the manifest build.

- Stimulus sequences: `seqs/sched_a.seq` (NO_OP_STRING "SEQ_A"), `sched_b.seq` ("SEQ_B"), `sched_long.seq` ("SEQ_L_START", R00:00:08 "SEQ_L_END"), compiled by `fprime-seqgen` (time base TB_DONT_CARE) into Ref's run directory before the run (entry gate).
- Out of scope: sequence file content/validity (`Svc.CmdSequencer`), parameter file integrity (`Svc.PrmDb`), DP buffer exhaustion (REQ-035, UT), two scheduler instances (REQ-040, UT).
entry_gates: - Stage-1 close: `fprime-util check` on `Svc/SeqScheduler` and `Ref/TimeBaseOverride` passes with every row of the SDD unit-test lists implemented.
- Image: Ref built from the manifest SHAs with `Svc.Version` enabled (CdhCore subtopology); `version.VERSION ALL` payloads are the manifest's describe strings (L0-1).

- Marker round-trip: `CdhCore.cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP_STRING("<id>")` echoed as `NoOpStringReceived(message=<id>)` once (L0-2); the event text `Received a NO-OP string=<id>` is the marker regex. Run-start markers use the `RFR <run> M/S <sha8>` string form.
- Downlink budget: ≤ 20 events/s over the Ref TCP link; the plan's densest window (L2-4) emits < 20 events total.
- Bench recipe: `bench.json` names the Ref binary, run directory (sequences and `/tmp/PrmDb.dat` beneath it), the GDS start command and a `reset` template that restarts the Ref process (L3-1).
- Parameter file: deleted before the run so L0-2 sees default rows.
- Run-level parameter: L0-2 sets `DONE_TIMEOUT_TICKS` = 30 before any dispatch; every later test assumes it.
levels: L0 provenance/feasibility · L2 functional · L3 persistence/reset · L4 endurance/performance · L5 fault paths · L6 negative controls · L7 final state for independent verification.

tests.title: Image identity
tests.purpose: Confirms the running Ref image is the manifest's build (Svc.Version payloads equal the pinned describe strings).
tests.setup: Ref started from the manifest build in its run directory; GDS attached; dictionary from the same build.
checks: version payloads == manifest describe (check function: FrameworkVersion/ProjectVersion text equal repos[].describe; 40-char truncation applies)
tests.evidence: EVRs FrameworkVersion / ProjectVersion / LibraryVersions beside manifest.json repos[].describe.

tests.title: Marker round-trip and idle table
tests.purpose: Proves the marker round-trips and the scheduler starts with eight pending, no due row and no override.
tests.setup: Fresh start; parameter file absent (default rows: all disabled). Sets the run-level DONE_TIMEOUT_TICKS = 30 (SDD: 0 is a test default) so any stuck row closes within 30 s.

rationale.text: NextRow = lowest index among enabled PENDING rows (condition-holding first, then earliest due); disabled rows excluded; 8 when none (SDD Table 7)

tests.evidence: Telemetry strip RowsPending/NextRow/OverrideTimeBase over the window; no scheduler EVR.

tests.title: Start-relative dispatch
tests.purpose: Proves a START_RELATIVE row dispatches its sequence once when time since start reaches the offset and is marked complete.
tests.setup: Row 0 disabled; seqs/sched_a.bin present (compiled by fprime-seqgen from sched_a.seq, TB_DONT_CARE). S = last(seqScheduler.SinceStart) read before the window.
checks: dispatch not early (check function: t(RowDispatched) - t(ENABLE_ROW sent) >= 3 s)

rationale.text: offset 5 s + 1 s run period + 1 s SinceStart read granularity + 1 s margin

tests.evidence: EVR sequence RowEdited×3 → RowDispatched(0) → cmdDisp NoOpStringReceived(SEQ_A) → CS_SequenceComplete → RowCompleted(0).

tests.title: Absolute dispatch
tests.purpose: Proves an ABSOLUTE row dispatches only while the system base equals its base, at its absolute time and not before.
tests.setup: Row 1 disabled; no override (Ref base TB_WORKSTATION_TIME); N = host UNIX seconds at send.

rationale.text: row base TB_SC_TIME ≠ system base TB_WORKSTATION_TIME for 6 s past the row time: not eligible (REQ-005); queued edits complete ≈2–3 s after N, so SET_TIME_BASE lands ≈N+9..10 and the row is 5–6 s late when the base appears, under LATE_LIMIT_SECONDS = 10 (margin ≥ 4 s)

tests.evidence: W1: no dispatch for 6 s while the base mismatches; W2: OverrideChanged → RowDispatched(1) within 3 s → SEQ_B → RowCompleted(1).

tests.title: Time-base-relative dispatch
tests.purpose: Proves a TIME_BASE_RELATIVE row waits for its base and dispatches the offset after the base is first reported.
tests.setup: Row 2 disabled; no override; Ref base TB_WORKSTATION_TIME.
checks: W2: dispatch not early (check function: t(RowDispatched) - t(SET_TIME_BASE sent) >= 4 s)

rationale.text: offset 5 s + 1 s to observe the base + 1 s run period + 1 s margin
NextRow = lowest index among enabled PENDING rows (condition-holding first, then earliest due); disabled rows excluded; 8 when none (SDD Table 7)

tests.evidence: W1: no dispatch for 8 s while the base is absent; W2: OverrideChanged → TimeBaseChanged → RowDispatched(2) ≈5 s later → restore.

tests.title: waitPrevious and lowest-index order
tests.purpose: Proves two rows due together dispatch lowest index first and a waitPrevious row waits for the running sequence to complete.
tests.setup: Rows 3 and 4 disabled; seqs/sched_long.bin (8 s) and sched_a.bin present; S = last(SinceStart).
tests.evidence: EVR order: RowDispatched(3) → SEQ_L_START → SEQ_L_END → RowCompleted(3) → RowDispatched(4) → SEQ_A → RowCompleted(4).

tests.title: cancelPrevious
tests.purpose: Proves a cancelPrevious row cancels the running scheduler sequence and dispatches after the cancelled completion is reported.
metrics: t(event seqScheduler.RowDispatched(index=6)) - t(event seqScheduler.RowCancelled(index=6, running=5)) <= 1 s

rationale.text: CmdSequencer reports a cancelled sequence as EXECUTION_ERROR on seqDone (CmdSequencerImpl.cpp CS_CANCEL path) — stage 2 confirms the response value

tests.evidence: EVR order: RowDispatched(5) → SEQ_L_START → RowCancelled(6,5) → CS_SequenceCanceled → RowFailed(5, EXECUTION_ERROR; row state CANCELLED) → RowDispatched(6) → SEQ_B; SEQ_L_END absent.

tests.title: Table dump
tests.purpose: Proves DUMP_TABLE writes a data product holding every row with its state.
tests.setup: Rows as left by L2-1..L2-5: 0 COMPLETE (sched_a, START_RELATIVE), 1 COMPLETE (sched_b, ABSOLUTE), 2 COMPLETE (sched_a, TIME_BASE_RELATIVE TB_SC_TIME), 3 COMPLETE (sched_long), 4 COMPLETE (sched_a, waitPrevious), 5 CANCELLED (sched_long), 6 COMPLETE (sched_b, cancelPrevious), 7 PENDING disabled (default); DataProducts subtopology running.
checks: dump matches the expected table (check function: parse the DP file named by FileWritten; 8 RowRecords; every field — enabled, mode, timeBase, seconds, useconds, waitPrevious, cancelPrevious, sequence, rowState — equals the Setup table)

rationale.text: exactly one container per DUMP_TABLE; no other DP producer is commanded in this test

tests.evidence: EVR FileWritten(bytes, file); the file itself (independent of the scheduler's own reporting) decoded by the check function.

tests.title: Second absolute row
tests.purpose: Proves a second ABSOLUTE row in the current base dispatches at its absolute time and completes.
tests.setup: Row 7 disabled; no override; N = host UNIX seconds at send.
tests.evidence: EVR RowDispatched(7) → SEQ_A → RowCompleted(7); DISABLE_ROW(7) at the end restores the default-like state for L2-6/L5-1.

tests.title: Time-base-relative row under a second base
tests.purpose: Proves a TIME_BASE_RELATIVE row for TB_PROC_TIME waits for that base and dispatches the offset after it is first reported.
tests.setup: Row 6 disabled (re-armed by the edits); no override.
tests.evidence: W1: no dispatch for 5 s; W2: TimeBaseChanged → RowDispatched(6) ≈3 s later → SEQ_B → RowCompleted(6).

tests.title: Persistence and start-relative across restart
tests.purpose: Proves a saved table survives a restart and a START_RELATIVE row dispatches the offset after the new start.
tests.setup: Rows 0..7 in their post-L2 states; /tmp/PrmDb.dat writable (int_config.json Svc.PrmDb.filename).
procedure: wait until CdhCore.version ProjectVersion EVR after restart
checks: W2: restart observed (check function: first(SinceStart) in W2 < last(SinceStart) in W1)
W2: unsaved edit lost (check function: DP row 7 sequence == parameter value, not seqs/sched_b.bin; row 7 disabled)

rationale.text: row 0 due 5 s after the ORIGINAL start is long past; it is only re-armed by the edits and must not dispatch before the restart because its lateness exceeds LATE_LIMIT_SECONDS — RowSkippedLate(0) in W1 is expected and ignored (edit re-arms again after restart from the saved parameter)
first sample after restart; bounds the new epoch

FSW time is host UNIX time, so a Ref restart has no clock fall-back and no exporter epoch boundary: R is reset:false by design; the restart is evidenced by the SinceStart fall-back and the Svc.Version startup EVR (plan decision 12, Q25)

tests.evidence: W1: TableSaved → PrmFileSaveComplete; R: FSW clock restart; W2: RowDispatched(0) within ≈5 s of first run cycle → SEQ_A → RowCompleted(0).

tests.title: Relative clocks under a time base change
tests.purpose: Proves SinceStart keeps accumulating and SinceBase restarts when the base changes, both advancing one second per run cycle over a 60 s strip.
tests.setup: No override; no enabled pending row due in the window; B = last(SinceBase), S = last(SinceStart) before the window.
checks: SinceBase restarts on each base entry (check function: a SinceBase sample <= 1 follows each TimeBaseChanged; SinceBase never decreases between them)
SinceStart continues across the change (check function: SinceStart non-decreasing over the whole window; delta(SinceStart) within ±3 s of the window duration)
SinceBase advances with the strip (check function: delta(SinceBase) between the two TimeBaseChanged events within ±3 s of their spacing)

rationale.text: 1 Hz run period; allow 5 missed downlink frames in 60 s

tests.evidence: Telemetry strips SinceStart (unbroken staircase) and SinceBase (two restarts) beside OverrideChanged/TimeBaseChanged EVRs.

tests.title: Late row skipped
tests.purpose: Proves a row first due more than LATE_LIMIT_SECONDS ago is skipped with a warning and never dispatched.
tests.setup: Row 7 disabled; LATE_LIMIT_SECONDS at default 10; N = host UNIX seconds.
tests.evidence: EVR RowSkippedLate(7, due, now) once; no RowDispatched; RowsSkipped steps to 1.

tests.title: Late start-relative row
tests.purpose: Proves a START_RELATIVE row whose offset is already more than LATE_LIMIT_SECONDS in the past is skipped, never dispatched.

tests.title: Completion timeout
tests.purpose: Proves an unreported end times out after DONE_TIMEOUT_TICKS and the late sequencer report is ignored as foreign.
tests.setup: Row 3 disabled; S = last(SinceStart); sched_long.bin (8 s).

rationale.text: the late CS_SequenceComplete arrives after the row is TIMED_OUT, so no row is unconfirmed-or-confirmed outstanding: it is ignored with ForeignSeqDone (REQ-024)

tests.evidence: EVR RowDispatched(3) → RowTimedOut(3) ≈3 s later → SEQ_L_END/CS_SequenceComplete ≈8 s later with no RowCompleted.

tests.title: Time base never seen
tests.purpose: Proves a row for a base not reported within BASE_WAIT_TICKS is skipped with a warning.
tests.setup: Row 2 disabled; Ref up longer than 5 run cycles; no override.
metrics: t(event seqScheduler.RowSkippedNoBase(index=2, timeBase=TB_PROC_TIME)) - t(seqScheduler.ENABLE_ROW sent) <= 3 s
tests.evidence: EVR RowSkippedNoBase(2, TB_PROC_TIME) once; no RowDispatched.

tests.title: Rejected edits
tests.purpose: Proves every Table 6 violation and the override of TB_DONT_CARE are rejected with a warning and change nothing.
tests.setup: Any table state with no row due; P = last(RowsPending) before the window.
tests.evidence: Five rejection EVRs, no RowEdited/RowDispatched/OverrideChanged; RowsPending flat.

tests.title: Rejections while a row runs
tests.purpose: Proves a running row cannot be edited while other rows can, and that bad-index, Table 6 and TB_DONT_CARE requests are rejected.
checks: event seqScheduler.RowDispatched(index=5) precedes event seqScheduler.RowRejected(index=5, reason=ROW_DISPATCHED)
tests.evidence: EVR RowDispatched(5) → RowRejected(5, ROW_DISPATCHED), RowEdited(6), RowRejected(9, BAD_INDEX), RowRejected(6, BAD_TIME_BASE), InvalidTimeBase → RowCompleted(5).

tests.title: Final state
tests.purpose: Leaves every row disabled and pending, no override, and a table dump the auditor decodes independently.
checks: final dump: 8 rows, every field as last set, all disabled, all PENDING (check function over the DP file named by FileWritten)

rationale.text: NextRow = lowest index among enabled PENDING rows (condition-holding first, then earliest due); disabled rows excluded; 8 when none (SDD Table 7)

tests.evidence: Final telemetry strip and the DP file (decoded by the auditor from the run directory, not from scheduler EVRs).

decision_log: 1. 2026-11-10 designer — deployment = Ref system deployment plus seqScheduler/timeBaseOverride (the human's request); no reduced deployment.

2. 2026-11-10 designer — marker = `CdhCore.cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP_STRING(<id>)` → `NoOpStringReceived` text `Received a NO-OP string=<id>`; the harness sender passes marker ids as strings (shell-quoted `str(arg)`).

3. 2026-11-10 designer — short event/command names are the Ref dictionary names minus the `Ref.` prefix (`seqScheduler.X`, `cmdSeq.X`); subtopology instances keep their prefix (`CdhCore.cmdDisp.X`, `FileHandling.prmDb.X`, `DataProducts.dpWriter.X`).

4. 2026-11-10 designer — sequences compiled with `fprime-seqgen` default time base TB_DONT_CARE so they run under any override (CmdSequencer `CS_TimeBaseMismatch` is skipped for TB_DONT_CARE — confirm at stage 2).

5. 2026-11-10 designer — telemetry `SinceStart`/`SinceBase` added to the FPP at test design to make START_RELATIVE rows testable live (L2-1/L2-4/L2-5/L5-2/L6-2 read S from telemetry); the design reviewers are told of the delta in their open round.
6. 2026-11-10 designer — L3 reset = restart the Ref process (bench `reset` template); `/tmp/PrmDb.dat` persists across it.
7. 2026-11-10 designer — final-state evidence = the L7-1 DP file decoded by the auditor from the run directory (independent of scheduler EVRs); `final_state.accepted_evidence` set accordingly.
8. 2026-11-10 designer — max_count = 2; six planted faults over seven tests (≥ 2 × max_count); one `uut-state` fault (`disturb_disable`, `persist_late_row`).

10. 2026-11-10 designer — design review round 1 ripple: row states split (COMPLETE/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT/SKIPPED_*), telemetry RowsFailed/NextMode, events ForeignSeqDone/QueueFull, synchronous DP get, seqStartIn attribution; checks updated in L0-2, L2-5, L2-6, L5-2, L7-1; no test added or removed.

11. 2026-11-10 designer — parameter-set command mnemonics (`seqScheduler.<PARAM>_PRM_SET`) are the fprime dictionary convention; confirm from the generated dictionary at stage 2 (design-review r2 low-confidence note).

9. 2026-11-10 designer — redundancy (revised r1 of system-test review): knob-free second tests L2-7 (004/005/014/023), L2-8 (009/010/011), L5-4 (017/018) added; REQ-002/-015/-020/-021/-027/-033 keep a single system test with an explicit waiver note; the waiver form is put to the human (Q23).

12. 2026-11-10 designer — system-test review r1: STD completeness uses helper `commands_sent_minus_seq` (sequence-issued NO-OPs are dispatched by cmdDisp but not in commands.jsonl); OpCodeError moved from STD into ABS, with ABS-REJ for the negative controls; every test declares ABS/ABS-REJ; run-level DONE_TIMEOUT_TICKS = 30 set in L0-2; L3-1 restart window is reset:false (wall-clock FSW time, Q25); L2-6/L7-1 dump checks compare every field; L2-2 adds the base-mismatch phase (REQ-005); L3-1 adds an unsaved edit (REQ-027); REQ-013 waived UT only; metrics predicates are matched at unseal and listed in fails.

13. 2026-11-10 designer — design gap found by the system-test reviewer: a row without waitPrevious due while another row is DISPATCHED now FAILS without dispatch (REQ-SEQSCHED-041, RowFailed(index, BUSY)); drop_wait_flag's signature re-derived accordingly.

14. 2026-11-10 designer — system-test review r2: helper counts sequence NO-OPs by the SEQ_ message prefix (markers are numeric); REQ-SEQSCHED-041 narrowed to rows with neither flag (cancelPrevious takes precedence); L2-2 W1 shortened to 6 s for a ≥4 s lateness margin; disturb_disable/no_cancel_flag fails re-derived; redundancy waiver form remains the human's call (Q23).

15. 2026-11-10 designer — system-test review r3 (post-bound, gate note G7): L2-5 metric sign corrected and added to no_cancel_flag.fails; SDD Behavior flag order aligned with REQ-022 (cancel before wait).

final_state.accepted_evidence: L7-1 DP file decoded by the auditor (8 RowRecords, all disabled/PENDING) plus the final telemetry strip
final_state.rationale: Ref is a host process; the DP file written by DataProducts.dpWriter is read from the run directory by the check function and again by the auditor, independently of the scheduler's own EVRs.
